key_insight: A modified quantum annealing eigensolver can reproduce magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants for light atoms, extending quantum-hardware results beyond ground-state energies.
engineering_relevance: This shows that near-term quantum annealers can be used as practical numerical solvers for small relativistic atomic-structure problems when paired with careful encoding and truncation.
method: Used a modified QAE with zooming and sigma-annealing on D-Wave hardware.
Encoded eigenvalues/eigenvectors with floating-point precision limited to three decimals (up to 10 qubits).
Applied CSF truncation for larger correlation spaces, keeping only the most influential configurations.
evidence_signal: Hardware runs on the D-Wave QPU matched GRASP benchmarks at the chosen precision for neutral Li, Li-like Be, neutral Na, and Na-like Mg, though accuracy varied with matrix size.
watch_item: The approach is currently limited to small Hamiltonians and reduced precision, so scalability and sensitivity to CSF truncation remain important concerns.
paper_title: Applications of quantum annealing to magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants: First results beyond energies for atoms
